watch.label: Glen Or Glenda (1953), directed by Edward D. Wood Jr. (about 71 min)

editorial:
Glen or Glenda is Ed Wood's directorial debut. It is a 1953 docudrama about cross-dressing, shot on a $20,000 budget in four days. Producer George Weiss commissioned it, and Screen Classics was the distributor. It is the only film Wood directed without also producing. Bela Lugosi appears in it, and Wood's girlfriend Dolores Fuller co-stars. William Lava wrote the uncredited music. The film is mostly stock footage in places. The Alan or Anne segment was added to meet the distributor's demand for sex-change content. It was released under several titles, including I Led Two Lives, He or She? and I Changed My Sex.

Its rights status is not settled in this dossier. The queue marks the renewal as probably absent, but I could not reach the Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes or a Copyright Office record to confirm it. Do the renewal check by hand before treating the print as free. The film also contains stock footage whose owners were not traced. Anything added by a modern release is a separate matter. That includes the 2009 colorized Legend Films edition and the 2020 restored HD print, whose terms I have not seen.
faq: Is the Internet Archive copy of Glen or Glenda safe to reuse?

Not confirmed yet. The queue suggests the 1953 copyright may never have been renewed, but this dossier has no primary record showing it. Search the US Copyright Office's public records (publicrecords.copyright.gov) for renewals filed around 1980 to 1982 before you reuse it. Even if no renewal turns up, the stock footage inside the film has not been cleared.
Can I use the colorized or restored versions?

Use the plain black-and-white print where you can. The 2009 colorized release and the 2020 restored HD print may include additions that carry their own rights. Check the terms of each release. Do not rip a copy-protected disc, because that can violate 17 U.S.C. 1201.
